label: rem:geodesic-vortices
title: Geodesic vortices: variational characterisation and stability
html:
Geodesics of the acoustic metric exactly map to the critical points of the q-deformed energy functional evaluated over closed curves in the state bundle \mathcal{S}.

The q-energy functional. For \varrho \colon S^1 \to \mathcal{S}:

  \mathcal{E}_q[\varrho]
  = 
  \oint_\varrho
  \bigl(
    \tfrac{1}{2}\lVert\dot\varrho^H\rVert^2
    + Q_q(\varrho)
    + \lVert F_A(\dot\varrho)\rVert^2
  \bigr)ds,

where \dot\varrho^H specifies the horizontal velocity, Q_q the quantum pressure, and F_A(\dot\varrho) the filament curvature.

Critical points are geodesics. Evaluating \delta\mathcal{E}_q / \delta\varrho = 0 produces

  \nabla_{\dot\varrho}\dot\varrho
  = -\nabla^\perp Q_q - \iota_{\dot\varrho}{*F_A}.

As q \to 1, Q_q \to 0 and the gauge term simplifies into Biot--Savart self-induction (the classical Hasimoto soliton).

Stability. The second variation \delta^2\mathcal{E}_q resolves via the weight-space decomposition:

  • Longitudinal (Cartan): Stable, carrying eigenvalues [k]_q^2 \hbar_q / L_q^2 (discrete spectrum).
  • Ladder (E_\pm): Protected by an energetic barrier \Delta E = \hbar_q([j\!+\!1]_q[j\!+\!2]_q - [j]_q[j\!+\!1]_q)/(2I_q) > 0 strictly when q > 1.
  • Gauge: Trivially zero (quotiented out by symmetry).

Index theorem. The Morse index of the fundamental vortex (j = 1/2) evaluates to zero: no subordinate energy state exists. The lightest fermion acts as the absolute minimum of \mathcal{E}_q within its topological class.

Connection to mass. \mathcal{E}_q[\gamma_0] = \oint_{\gamma_0} \lVert\nabla_A q\rVert \cdot \lVert L \wedge F^+\rVert \propto m explicitly generates the mass identity. The static limit of \mathcal{E}_q functions as the geometric drag.
